record.title: NVIDIA documents NVKE Kubernetes AI conformance testing on two GB200 workers
record.summary: NVIDIA's AICR v1.2.0 release includes an NVKE GB200 training/Kubeflow recipe and publishes a Kubernetes v1.36 AI conformance submission. In the linked submission, NVIDIA says it collected evidence on Oct 27–28, 2026 using NVKE v0.22.0 and Kubernetes v1.36.3 on two ARM64 GB200 workers with eight GPUs. The results matrix marks seven applicable MUST requirements as passed and cluster autoscaling as not applicable under the operator-controlled scaling design. These are vendor-authored results for the described configuration; independent replay or external CNCF acceptance was not established in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NVIDIA published AICR v1.2.0 on 2 November 2026; the release includes an NVKE GB200 training/Kubeflow recipe and a Kubernetes v1.36 AI conformance submission.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: NVIDIA's submission says the NVKE v0.22.0 configuration was tested on Kubernetes v1.36.3 with two ARM64 GB200 workers and eight GPUs; it marks seven applicable AI conformance MUST requirements as implemented and passed, while marking cluster autoscaling not applicable because scaling is operator-controlled.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The inspected materials do not establish independent replay of the evidence, external CNCF acceptance of this submission, production performance beyond the described test configuration, or general conformance across other hardware and deployments.

evidence_gaps.description: The committed conformance evidence files and exact recipe/configuration have not been fully inspected or replayed by an independent operator; external CNCF acceptance was not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported configuration and qualification evidence generalize, tested Kubernetes recipes for GPU clusters could lower integration effort and make AI infrastructure requirements more reproducible. This account is limited to NVIDIA's NVKE v0.22.0 GB200 configuration and its vendor-authored conformance submission; external acceptance, independent reproduction and broader service performance are not established.
limitations: The submission and PASS results are NVIDIA-authored; independent reproduction was not located in this bounded review.
The README describes one NVKE v0.22.0/Kubernetes v1.36.3 configuration with two ARM64 GB200 workers and eight GPUs; it does not establish general platform compatibility.
Cluster autoscaling is explicitly marked not applicable because the operator controls scaling; it is not a passed workload-driven autoscaling result.
A public conformance submission is not evidence that CNCF accepted or certified the platform.
The underlying evidence files were not fully inspected or replayed here, and no external service-performance measurement was established.

technical.claimed_result: The NVIDIA submission reports seven applicable Kubernetes v1.36 AI conformance MUST requirements passed on its NVKE/GB200 test configuration; workload-driven cluster autoscaling is listed as not applicable because NVKE uses operator-controlled scaling.
technical.demonstrated_result: NVIDIA publicly released AICR v1.2.0 and merged a submission containing PRODUCT.yaml, a results README and supporting evidence files. The pull-request summary describes the recorded test regime and result matrix; the underlying evidence was not independently replayed here.
technical.implementation_status: The NVKE GB200 training/Kubeflow recipe and the vendor's conformance-submission documentation are publicly available in the AICR v1.2.0 release/repository. External CNCF acceptance of the submission is not established.
technical.mechanism: AICR packages versioned GPU-cluster recipes. The described NVKE setup combines a GB200 training/Kubeflow recipe with Agentgateway and uses behavioral tests for scheduling, GPU access isolation, metrics, gateway traffic, operator reconciliation and GPU-metric scaling.
technical.regime: NVIDIA NVKE v0.22.0 on Kubernetes v1.36.3, with two ARM64 GB200 workers and eight GPUs; the submission says evidence collection occurred 27–28 October 2026. This does not cover other cluster providers or hardware.
technical.reproducibility: The PR includes sanitized evidence files and configuration metadata, but those files were not fully inspected or independently executed in this review. The account remains vendor-reported.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched cross-platform or independent GB200 comparison was reported. This record describes a single vendor-authored conformance submission, not comparative performance.

brief.title: NVIDIA documents NVKE Kubernetes AI conformance testing on two GB200 workers
brief.why_it_matters: A detailed, recipe-linked conformance submission can make GPU-cluster integration requirements and evidence more inspectable. The demonstrated scope is one NVIDIA NVKE/GB200 configuration and NVIDIA's submitted results; it does not establish external certification, broader interoperability or production service performance.
